title: kv: strided-evictor with adaptive vacancy smoothing and async spill controller
author: Asha Menon
description: Motivation: tenant-level allocation hotspots and micro-fragmentation cause frequent small evictions and suboptimal slab utilization under mixed workloads (short-chat QPS + long-generation tails). This PR introduces a three-part memory-management strategy to reduce fragmentation, smooth eviction storms, and avoid synchronous spill-related latency spikes. Design: 1) Strided Evictor: an eviction selection strategy that walks slab memory in deterministic strides (configurable stride size) to avoid localized hot-slot thrashing. The evictor biases by age + recency but enforces stride gaps to distribute evictions across segments, reducing contiguous free-run fragmentation. 2) Adaptive Vacancy Smoothing: a background compaction-friendly pass that opportunistically migrates cold entries into coalesced runs to create larger contiguous free regions for future large allocations. It uses a sampled heatmap per slab class and applies a moving-average vacancy threshold to decide migration windows. Smoothing runs are throttled by CPU/IO headroom heuristics to ensure steady-state costs remain negligible. 3) Async Spill Controller: when memory pressure is sustained and vacancy smoothing cannot make enough room, we initiate asynchronous, rate-limited spill-to-disk for selected cold ranges rather than immediate eviction. The controller coordinates with the KV spill subsystem to batch spill jobs and backpressure upstream allocation loops so we avoid synchronous eviction stalls. Implementation highlights: - New kv/evict/strided_evictor.cc/.h implementing configurable stride, eviction policy hooks, and unit-tested determinism. - Vacancy smoother implemented as kv/maintenance/vacancy_smoother.{cc,h} with a lightweight sampling heatmap and pluggable cost model. - Async spill controller in kv/spill/async_controller.{cc,h} with a spill job queue, backpressure tokens, and integration points for disk spill workers. - Runtime knobs exposed via config schema: kv.eviction.stride_size, kv.smoother.enabled/interval/cpu_limit, kv.spill.async_threshold/batch_size. - Bench harness and microbenchmarks added under benchmark/kv to reproduce fragmentation regressions. Tests & validation: unit tests for deterministic eviction, integration tests for smoother throttling, and end-to-end perf runs in benchmark-lab pipeline. Benchmarks: on mixed short+long workload (50k req/s synthetic mix) we saw: - 32% reduction in eviction rate (evictions/sec) - 18% decrease in P99 tail latency for short requests when under 70% util - 12% lower average memory amplification (less wasted holes) Rollout plan: feature gated under kv.smoother.enabled=false by default; gradually enable on low-risk clusters, monitor eviction_rate and allocator_free_run_median. Backout toggle added. Related: this PR complements ENG-6421 (allocator refactor) and relies on the spill API added in ENG-6103. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked in PR comments - [x] Unit tests - [x] Bench harness and data - [x] Runtime config knobs - [x] Migration/rollback plan

review_comments: Diego Ramos: Nice approach — can you quantify CPU cost of smoothing under steady load? Suggest adding a CPU budget meter to avoid oscillation.
Asha Menon: Added a cpu_limit knob and a budget meter; updated integration tests to assert smoother backs off when cpu usage > threshold.
Lena O'Hara: Async spill looks promising. Concern: rehydration latency for spilled ranges. Please add metrics for spill/read latency and a priority inversion guard.
Asha Menon: Added spill_read_latency and spill_queue_wait metrics; introduced a priority inversion check to prefer rehydration for recent evicted keys.
Marcus Li: Tests failing on macOS runners (atomic order). Fixed and pushed a patch to use portable atomics.
Diego Ramos: Running a canary on perf-cluster-2 with kv.smoother.enabled=true showed eviction_rate drop but occasional CPU spikes — LGTM behind feature flag. Approving.
merge_details: Merged via squash on 2025-02-20 by release-bot. Squash commit message includes benchmark summary and rollout instructions.
release_notes: Improves KV cache fragmentation and reduces eviction storms by introducing a strided eviction policy, background vacancy smoothing, and an asynchronous spill controller. Feature is off by default and can be enabled via kv.smoother.enabled; recommended to enable gradually and observe eviction_rate and allocator_free_run_median metrics.
notes_for_ops: Default disabled: kv.smoother.enabled=false. When enabling set kv.smoother.cpu_limit <= 10% initially.
Monitor metrics: kv.evictions_per_minute, kv.spill_queue_length, kv.spill_read_latency, allocator_free_run_median.
